ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a DC power supply labeled 12 V; the positive terminal of the power supply is connected through a 100 μH inductor to the switching node; this node is connected downward to MOSFET Q and then to the lower common loop, and connected rightward through a diode to the output terminal; a 470 μF capacitor and a 20 Ω resistor load are connected in parallel at the output terminal. This structure is a typical step-up chopper, namely a boost converter. Reasoning: It is known that the duty cycle of the MOSFET is D = 0.4, and all components are ideal. According to the voltage gain of an ideal continuous conduction mode boost converter, Vout = Vin / (1 - D) = 12 / (1 - 0.4) = 20 V. The 20 Ω load current is Iout = Vout / R = 20 / 20 = 1 A, so the output power Pout = 20 V × 1 A = 20 W. In an ideal converter, Pin = Pout, so the average source current Is_avg = Pin / Vin = 20 / 12 = 5/3 A.

method.method_draft: First identify the image as a boost converter. From the text, use D = 0.4, fs = 250 kHz, and ideal operation. Apply the CCM boost gain: Vout = 12/(1-0.4) = 20 V. The 20 Ω load then draws Iout = 20/20 = 1 A, so Pout = 20 W. Since the converter is ideal, Pin = Pout, hence the average source current is Is_avg = 20/12 = 5/3 A.

推理：已知 MOSFET 的占空比 D = 0.4，所有元件理想。按理想连续导通模式 boost 变换器电压增益，Vout = Vin / (1 - D) = 12 / (1 - 0.4) = 20 V。20 Ω 负载电流为 Iout = Vout / R = 20 / 20 = 1 A，因此输出功率 Pout = 20 V × 1 A = 20 W。理想变换器中 Pin = Pout，所以平均源电流 Is_avg = Pin / Vin = 20 / 12 = 5/3 A。

method.method_draft: Describe the two switch states from the circuit. During Q ON, the inductor is charged from the 12 V source and the diode is off, so vL = 12 V. During Q OFF, the inductor delivers energy through the diode to the output, so vL = 12 - Vout. Apply volt-second balance: D(12) + (1-D)(12 - Vout) = 0 with D = 0.4, giving Vout = 20 V. The load current is Iout = Vout/20 = 1 A. Since the diode conducts only for the off fraction 1-D and carries the inductor current in that interval, Iout = (1-D) IL_avg. Thus IL_avg = 1/0.6 = 5/3 A. Because the source is in series with the inductor in the image, the average source current equals IL_avg.
